chapter: Instruments, own band and the Eureka
title: Goodbyes and his children
summary: Allen thanks Williams; Williams says he had six children, none became bandsmen.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Well, we'd like to come back and talk to you again.
Okay, we thank you, Mary. Bye. Bye.
Bye. That's my oldest boy. I lost a boy since I've been here. He's the third boy. My baby boy in Brooklyn, New York.
I had six. I had four boys and two girls.
Did any of them play music?

I had one back a time to play guitar, somebody, you don't fool with it much. That's it with my girl. When I was living on the Jantilly Street, I had this boy on clarinet, the next boy on drum, and the girl on the violin. So when I moved from Jantilly Street and moved back here, they just put it down. They wouldn't fool it at all. I bought the youngest girl the piano. She ain't never learned that soul to play.
They never did go out and play with bands or anything?
No. Oh no, they never learned good enough to play with no bands. Well, let's see.
